content:
The [W-4 Withholding Calculator](/w-4-withholding-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Estimate federal tax withheld from each paycheck under the 2025 W-4 method. Enter your gross pay per paycheck, how often are you paid?, filing status, qualifying children under 17 and other dependents and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Estimate the federal income tax withheld from each paycheck using the 2025 W-4 method: your pay is annualised, the standard deduction (Single $15,750; married filing jointly $31,500; head of household $23,625) and dependent credits ($2,000 per qualifying child under 17, $500 per other dependent) are subtracted, the 2025 brackets are applied, and the result is divided back across your pay periods. This is an estimate based on the 2025 US federal brackets and standard deduction. It is not tax advice — your real tax depends on credits, state rules and your full situation, so check important figures with a tax professional.

## How to use the W-4 Withholding Calculator

Start by entering your gross pay per paycheck ($), then choosing your how often are you paid? from the list, choosing your filing status from the list, entering your qualifying children under 17 and finally entering your other dependents. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter your gross pay per paycheck and how often you are paid.
2. Choose your filing status and count your dependents.
3. Read the estimated withholding per paycheck and for the year.

## Formula

Annual gross = pay per period × periods per year. Taxable income = annual gross − standard deduction − dependent credits. Federal tax uses the 2025 brackets (10% to $11,925, 12% to $48,475, 22% to $103,350 for a single filer). Withholding per paycheck = annual tax ÷ periods per year.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [W-4 Withholding Calculator](/w-4-withholding-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A single filer paid $2,500 every two weeks earns $65,000 a year. After the $15,750 standard deduction, taxable income is $49,250 and the estimated federal tax is $5,749 a year — about $221.12 withheld per paycheck. Try the same figures in the [W-4 Withholding Calculator](/w-4-withholding-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Gross pay per paycheck: 2500 $, How often are you paid?: Every two weeks (26 paychecks), Filing status: Single, Qualifying children under 17: 0, Other dependents: 0), the [W-4 Withholding Calculator](/w-4-withholding-calculator) returns Federal withholding per paycheck: $221.12, Annual federal tax (estimated): $5,749, Annual gross pay: $65,000, Taxable income: $49,250, Marginal bracket: 22%, Net per paycheck (federal tax only): $2,278.88 — before state tax, FICA and deductions. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## What the W-4 does

The W-4 tells your employer how much federal tax to take from each paycheck. It accounts for your filing status, dependents, multiple jobs and other adjustments. This calculator follows the same annualised method the IRS tables use: it annualises your pay, subtracts the standard deduction and dependent credits, applies the brackets, and divides back across your pay periods. Real withholding can differ with bonuses, multiple jobs or itemised deductions.

## Why withholding is not your tax bill

Withholding is a prepayment, not the final answer. At tax time you compare what was withheld with what you actually owe: too much withheld means a refund, too little means a balance due (and possibly a penalty). If the estimate here is far from your real paycheck, check your W-4 — a new job, a raise, a marriage or a new child are all reasons to update it.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- A big refund means you lent the government money interest-free all year.
- Update your W-4 after a new job, a raise, a marriage or a new child.
- This covers federal tax only — state tax and FICA come out separately.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is federal withholding?

The federal income tax your employer takes from each paycheck and sends to the IRS on your behalf. It is a prepayment of the tax you will owe for the year. Try it with your own numbers in the [W-4 Withholding Calculator](/w-4-withholding-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How is withholding calculated?

Your pay is annualised, the standard deduction and dependent credits are subtracted, the 2025 tax brackets are applied, and the result is divided across your pay periods. Try it with your own numbers in the [W-4 Withholding Calculator](/w-4-withholding-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why is my withholding different from this estimate?

Real withholding follows IRS tables and your exact W-4, including multiple jobs, extra withholding and itemised deductions this calculator cannot see. Use the result as a close estimate. Try it with your own numbers in the [W-4 Withholding Calculator](/w-4-withholding-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does this include state tax or Social Security?

No — this is federal income tax only. State tax, Social Security and Medicare are withheld separately. Try it with your own numbers in the [W-4 Withholding Calculator](/w-4-withholding-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
